An idea was formed recently by me and some other over on "the other site" and I've been working quietly myself lately to implement a website.

The whole idea of a website was spurred by this imgur post.

My original idea sounded something like this:

Make a PCMR rating website. Everyone can submit their own scores on any game using the metric proposed by OP. But the genius part is that you can also set your own preferred weights on the ratings so that games will come custom-reviewed for you only! When you score a game you simply give each category a score of 0-100, consider each metric as objectively as possible. When you look for games however it shows the accumulated ratings weighted for your own personal preferences. For instance you might want to weight controls an 8 because it's very important to you. Someone else however wants DLC to be a 9 because they're very frugal.

In short the whole idea of this website is simple:

  1. All users can objectively rate games on the metrics proposed by /u/BallisticGE0RGE and improved by /u/macnetic.
  2. Users can search/browse games using their own customized weights for categories. Eg, if you're frugal you might be concerned with DLCs. Others might rate controls very important. Others yet again cannot possibly play a game without modding.

The implementation I'm working on is based on the python framework Django and it uses a PostGreSQL database backend. I have a Debian VPS server configured (professionally hosted) and the whole project is hosted on Github.

Ideally I'd like 1-2 contributors who's comfortable coding in Python with the Django framework. Myself I'm quite decent at coding but it's not what I primarily work with (I'm an IT consultant for a large health care provider).

I'm also using the Bootflat HTML/CSS framework and I believe I've found someone with experience who will aid with the design.

Check it out and let me know if you feel like helping out :) http://pcmr.co/ratings/ & https://github.com/the--dud/pcmr_co

Art, real art; The kind you walk into a museum and have to stare at for a moment to begin to focus on, isn’t something you stumble on every day. It’s the deliberate creation of focused autists, or near autists, who can do nothing but create that art. They focus hundreds, or thousands, of hours on the subject and the object of their art. Creating a rare composition.

In some rare cases their genius is realized in their lifetime, in most cases it’s discovered only after they have spent a lifetime creating, and honing their brilliance.

Rarely, very rarely, brilliance is discovered before the artist has been eddied to the tapestry of the next life, and when that happens the princes of this life will bring them into their employ.

Darren Calisto knew that Sal Matano was an artist, or at least the evidence led him to believe so. The story that his brother had fed him definitely made it appear that Salvatore was the author of the last great single attributable attack in the 20th century.

The International Monetary Fund’s Board of Governors had been suspected of wrongdoing. Ever since the collapse of the Japanese Economy in the late 90s it was suspected the IMF had been behind asset bubble. It was revealed by an “anonymous” hacker that the IMF board of governors had been directly responsible for bank to bank interest fluctuations.

The shameful exposure had led to the resignation of two of the longest standing IMF board members, and a large loss in confidence for the IMF. It had all been because of Sal. Now, no one really knew this. Sal held a high level of confidence that his contracts and Government clearances had left him relatively immune from any prosecution associated with the break in. Sitting at the prompt for the IMF central database had certainly been tempting.

He knew better, and had finished the job and exited. That was the last he had thought of it until a year ago when he had gotten the call.

“Salvatore Matano?” The strangely familiar voice had said.

“Yes, this is he.” Sal stomach was tightening even though he couldn’t place the voice.

“This is Darren Calisto. I’m calling to interview you for the position of Information Security Specialist.”

It had gone well, Sal had been working for Darren for the better part of seven years. The company had done well, creating military drones for any number of applications. Sal had made sure the company was able to operate those drones on behalf of the government and Darren had made sure to provide Sal with the resources he needed to continue protecting their resources.

It had been a win win so far. At least, until that August.

It had all started with an email, a hungarian immigrant and a command that dated back to the early 1990s and the birth of the networked PC.

Well no, that's not fair. It really started with a phone call.

"Salvatore?" The voice said formally.

"Yes?" Sal spat out, in the middle of what was turning into a particularly bad Thursday.

"This is Matthew Watkins from Intertron. We have some evidence that your company has been compromised. The data we have found on a data-drop has your companies usernames and password hashes."

Well Shit. Sal thought. It was bound to happen, we have too many people to avoid this kind of crap anymore.

"Can you provide me any intelligence as to the time, or the names of the systems involved?" Sal asked without letting his voice crack. At least, he didn't think it cracked.

After a pause, the other side of the line came back to life.

"We've sent it over. Let us know if you find anything else regarding this investigation."

Sal wasn't sure what he would find, but he was determined to find something.
